Dear Customer,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Lori from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

I apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused, but do not worry, we will do our best to help you.

All TOPENS products are backed by a 12-month warranty. Checked with our engineer, please help us do some tests to find out the problem, so that we can provide corresponding help.

1. Please measure the voltage of the +BAT- terminals (11# and 12#) on the control board to see whether it is above 22VDC. If so, please proceed to test 2. If the voltage is below 22VDC, please check whether the output voltage of the adapter is 36VDC. If so, disconnect the batteries from the control board and measure the output voltage of the batteries to see whether it is above 22VDC. If the voltage of the batteries is also below 22VDC, please keep the batteries charged fully to try it again. If it still cannot work, please check the batteries. Kindly note that a 24V 12Ah battery (or 2pcs 12V batteries connected in series may function as 24V) is required to power the gate opener. Marine or Automotive type battery is compatible.

2. Disconnect all accessories from the control board first (just leave the power source and the arm). And disable the photocell function by turning the dip switch #3 off. Then erase all remotes codes from the control board and reprogram them to have a try. If it fails, please instantaneously short (plug the wire in, then pull it out immediately) the push button terminals (4# and 5#) to check whether the opener can work. How to instantaneously short the “O/S/C COM” terminals: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VdDhyHZxmpQE5pG7BYHOJi5GYb7iZHFS/view?usp=sharing

3. If there is still no luck, please release the clutches on the arm and push the gate to the middle position firstly. And engage the clutches and press the remote to see whether the gate can run towards the both directions. If it still doesn’t help, please go on the troubleshooting below.

4. Please check the motor. Connect the red & black wires of the arm to the DC 24V power source directly, the motor should run, and then exchange the polarity of the wires, the motor should run in the opposite direction. If the motor runs in both directions, the motor itself is good. Please connect the black & red wires back to the control board and check step 5.

5. Disconnect the BLUE, GREEN & YELLOW wires of the faulty arm from the control board, use two jumper wires to short the ULT, COM & DLT terminals to which the wires were connected, and then press the remote to operate the gate opener to see whether it can work.

Please let me know the result one by one.

Videos showing the problem and pictures of the whole control board are much appreciated for further judgement. You can directly send the video to my E-mail via the attachment. If the sending is not successful, please share the photo or video link through dropbox, icloud or google drive. Thanks for your understanding and cooperation.

And also please reply your specific SHIPPING ADDRESS with zip code and confirm PHONE # available for further assistance.

Thank you again for being a valued customer! Your complete satisfaction is what we strive for. We at TOPENS are always standing by and ready to help.

Best regards,
Lori

If the arm is stuck in the fully extended position and the moving-rod does not retract:

1. Disengage the clutch and manually push the moving-rod to the middle position. Then, press the remote control to test for movement.
2. If the arm still does not move, re-engage the clutch and detach the arm from the gate. While pushing the moving-rod inward, rotate the front mount clockwise. If the arm begins to move, the screw nut may have disengaged from the screw rod at the far end. Once the arm is back in the middle position, use the remote control to test operation again.
3. Once the arm functions properly, use a screwdriver to loosen the screw on Limit Switch B. Slide the switch slightly inward and re-tighten the screw to prevent future over-extension.

If the opener arm is partially extended or fully retracted and the moving-rod does not move despite the motor activation:

4. Ensure that the clutch is fully and correctly engaged. If engagement appears normal, disassemble the opener arm and check whether clutch components (Part B and Part C) are properly aligned. If not, manually rotate the front mount until proper alignment is achieved.
5. Verify the connection between the screw rod and the clutch component with bearing (Part C). Also inspect the moving-rod’s screw nut for signs of damage or excessive wear.
6. If all visible components appear intact and operational, but abnormal or excessive noise is present in the motor area, the issue may lie within the motor’s reduction gearbox. In this case, please dismantle the gearbox of the motor and check the gears inside.

Dear Nick,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Joyce from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

Thank you for your interest in our gate openers! I am happy to help you choose the right models for your setup. Here is a breakdown of the key differences between the models you asked about.

The main differences come down to motor power, gate capacity, and holding force:
- **AT1202 / AT602:** These are both 24V DC ram-style arm actuators. The AT1202 is our heavy-duty model designed for gates up to 300 kg (660 lbs) per leaf. The AT602 is a medium-duty model for gates up to 250 kg (550 lbs) per leaf. Both offer excellent holding force for long, heavy gates.
- **A8132:** This is an electro-mechanical actuator, also 24V DC, for gates up to 300 kg (660 lbs) per leaf. It has a more industrial design and is incredibly robust, but the installation is slightly different from the AT series.
- **KD902 / KD702:** These are the best sellers. The KD902 is our heavy-duty articulated arm kit for gates up to 300 kg (660 lbs) per leaf. The KD702 is a medium-duty model for gates up to 250 kg (550 lbs) per leaf. The key benefit of the KD series is the soft start and soft stop functionality, making operation very smooth and quiet. For your described gate weight of 20-30 kg, any of these models is more than powerful enough.

Given that your gates are quite light (20-30 kg), the **KD702** would be an excellent choice. It will operate very smoothly and quietly, and the dual kit comes with everything you need including two arms, a control box, and all necessary accessories.

Regarding your control questions:
Each gate will have its own opener arm, and both arms connect to a single dual control box. The M12 remote controls included in the kit can be programmed to open either one gate, or both gates simultaneously. With your TC148 switches and TC175P touch panels, you can wire each to open either a single gate for private access, or both gates for shared access, depending on your wiring configuration. The TC196 WiFi remote works the same way—it replaces a remote control and can be programmed in the app to trigger the full dual-gate cycle.

Here is a link to the KD702 on Amazon UK for your reference: https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B07CLQVXDP

If you have any other questions before placing your order, please don't hesitate to ask.

Best regards,
Joyce
TOPENS Customer Service Team

Dear Customer,

Thank you for contacting TOPENS. This is Joyce from TOPENS Customer Service Team. It will be a pleasure to assist you today.

I apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused, but do not worry, we will do our best to help you. All TOPENS products are backed by a 12-month warranty.

Checked with our engineer, please help us do some tests to find out the problem, so that we can provide corresponding help.

1. First, please disconnect all wired accessories from the control board (just leave the power source and the arm). Disable the photocell function by turning DIP switch #5 off, and ensure that the jumper wire connected between the EDGE and GND (terminal #7 & #8) is securely fastened. Then observe if the gate will run randomly without the switch connected. I know you've already tested with a jumper wire between #4 and #5 and it worked normally, so the control board itself is likely fine.

2. With the switch still disconnected, please use a piece of wire to make an instant short between terminal #4 and #5 on the control board—that means plug the wire in and pull it out immediately, do not leave it connected as a continuous jumper. This simulates a proper retractive/dry-contact pulse. Then observe whether the gate runs a normal single cycle or starts cycling erratically.

3. If the instant-short test works normally, the issue is with the switch or its wiring. Your switch must provide a true dry contact momentary closure (COM and L1). Please check with a multimeter set to continuity: with the switch at rest, there should be no continuity between COM and L1. When you press and hold the switch, continuity should close; when you release, it should immediately break again. If the switch maintains continuity or chatters, it will cause the cycling you're seeing. Also please check whether the shielded armored cable has any stray strand or moisture bridging the cores, which could create a permanent or intermittent connection.

4. If the instant-short test also causes erratic cycling, please reprogram the remote controls: remove all existing remote codes from the control board, then reprogram the remotes. Operate the gate again to see if the random opening issue is resolved.

Please let me know the result one by one. Since your video is too large, you can share it via Dropbox, iCloud, or Google Drive link, and please also send clear photos of the control board wiring and your switch connections.

Lastly, kindly reply with your specific SHIPPING ADDRESS with zip code and confirm your PHONE # for further assistance if needed.
